blocks.text: In this chapter we explore the architecture and working of the kidneys, and the life-saving technologies used when this system weakens.

blocks.title: Excretion
blocks.text: Excretion is the process by which an organism eliminates its metabolic wastes: nitrogenous wastes, extra water and extra salts. In humans the urinary (excretory) system is responsible for it.

items: Nitrogenous waste removal: filtering out urea, the nitrogenous waste of protein breakdown made in the liver.
Osmoregulation: keeping the water-to-salt balance of the blood by adjusting how much water is reabsorbed or excreted.
pH and ion regulation: balancing sodium, potassium and hydrogen ions to keep the blood slightly basic, around pH 7.4.

Two kidneys, high in the abdominal cavity on either side of the vertebral column, between the 12th thoracic and 3rd lumbar vertebrae. Because of the liver the right kidney is slightly lower and smaller than the left. The 11th and 12th ribs partly protect their upper parts.
Two ureters, tubes about 25 cm long. Each begins at the funnel-shaped renal pelvis of its kidney and carries urine down to the bladder.
One urinary bladder, a hollow, stretchable muscular organ in the pelvic cavity that stores urine.
One urethra, the tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body.

blocks.alt: Left: the urinary organs from the front, two bean-shaped kidneys with adrenal glands on top beside the aorta and inferior vena cava, the right kidney a little lower, ureters running down to the urinary bladder in the pelvic cavity and the urethra below it. Right: a kidney cut open, showing the renal capsule, the outer cortex, the inner medulla with cone-shaped pyramids, the funnel-shaped renal pelvis, and the renal artery, renal vein and ureter at the hilum.
blocks.caption: The human urinary system and the inside of a kidney (original diagram after Figures 14.1 and 14.2).
blocks.long_description: The urinary system is two kidneys, two ureters, one urinary bladder and one urethra. The kidneys lie high in the abdomen on either side of the vertebral column, between the 12th thoracic and 3rd lumbar vertebrae; the right one is a little lower and smaller because of the liver. Each ureter, about 25 cm long, starts at the renal pelvis and carries urine to the bladder, a stretchable muscular store in the pelvic cavity; the urethra takes urine out of the body. Inside the kidney the cortex makes about a third of the mass and the medulla, with its renal pyramids, about two thirds; urine collects in the renal pelvis and leaves through the ureter at the hilum, where the renal artery enters and the renal vein leaves.

blocks.title: Critical thinking
blocks.text: Why is the large intestine not classed as a major excretory organ? Excretion removes metabolic wastes, made by the body's own chemistry; faeces are mostly undigested food that never entered the body's cells, so passing them is egestion. (This answer is general biology, not printed in the book.)

blocks.prompt: List the organs of the urinary system in the order urine passes through them.
blocks.explanation: Kidneys (urine forms and collects in the renal pelvis), ureters, urinary bladder, urethra.

items: Excretion removes metabolic wastes; the urinary system removes urea, osmoregulates and keeps blood pH near 7.4.
Organs: 2 kidneys, 2 ureters (25 cm), bladder, urethra; right kidney lower and smaller.
